AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is meat kept out of a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the compost too dry
   B. It kills the soil
   C. It attracts rats and flies and smells bad
   D. It turns into plastic

2. Which waste should NOT be put in a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Chicken droppings
   B. Fresh grass
   C. Plastic bags
   D. Banana peelings

3. Why is a compost heap turned with a fork? (1 mark)
   A. To add plastic
   B. To remove all the water
   C. To let in air and mix the materials
   D. To make it smaller

4. What word describes manure made from once-living things? (1 mark)
   A. Mineral only
   B. Plastic
   C. Metal
   D. Organic

5. Why does drip irrigation save water? (1 mark)
   A. It uses more water than a hose
   B. It wets the paths between plants
   C. Water goes close to the roots so little is wasted
   D. It waters at midday

6. What is the best time of day to water crops? (1 mark)
   A. Midnight only
   B. Noon
   C. Never
   D. Early morning or late afternoon

7. What is drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing water from a bucket quickly
   B. Spraying water high into the air
   C. Flooding the whole field
   D. Letting water fall slowly drop by drop near the roots

8. Which is a benefit of drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. The leaves get very wet
   B. Fewer weeds grow between plants
   C. More weeds grow
   D. Water is wasted

9. Which fuel comes in a metal cylinder? (1 mark)
   A. Gas
   B. Charcoal
   C. Firewood
   D. Dung cakes

10. Why is wet firewood a poor fuel? (1 mark)
   A. It lasts forever
   B. It burns very hot
   C. It has no smoke
   D. It makes a lot of smoke and gives little heat

11. How can a family get firewood without destroying forests? (1 mark)
   A. Burn grass
   B. Cut young trees only
   C. Plant trees on their own land and replace those cut
   D. Cut trees from forests at night

12. What should you do if you smell gas in the kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. Close the cylinder valve and open windows and doors
   B. Light a match to see
   C. Switch on many lights
   D. Cover your nose and cook

13. Which part holds the head of the scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. The tin
   B. The fence
   C. The dry grass on the ground
   D. The top of the pole

14. Which person is protecting wildlife? (1 mark)
   A. A person who burns a forest
   B. A person who poisons birds
   C. A hunter who sets a trap
   D. A learner who reports poaching to a wildlife officer

15. Why is it wrong to kill every bird that visits a field? (1 mark)
   A. Birds are always good
   B. Birds cannot eat crops
   C. Birds also eat harmful insects and are part of nature
   D. Birds pay tax

16. Which tool should an adult use to help fix the scarecrow pole? (1 mark)
   A. A bare hand only
   B. A knife on the pole
   C. A hammer or heavy stone to push it in
   D. A tin of paint

17. Which tool gives gentle watering of a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. Cup thrown from far
   B. Bucket poured fast
   C. Hose without a nozzle
   D. Watering can with a fine rose

18. Which crop is established by direct sowing of tiny seeds? (1 mark)
   A. Banana
   B. Carrot
   C. Sweet potato
   D. Mango

19. Why do we mix tiny seeds with dry sand? (1 mark)
   A. To kill germs
   B. To make them wet
   C. To spread them thinly and evenly
   D. To make them heavy

20. Why are weeds removed from the seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. They add manure
   B. They take water, light and food from the crop
   C. They protect seedlings from rain
   D. They are colourful

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Name two things that should never be put in a compost heap and say why. (2 marks)

22. Give two ways in which drip irrigation saves water. (2 marks)

23. Give two reasons why we should not kill wild animals that eat crops. (2 marks)

24. Explain what is meant by direct sowing. (2 marks)

25. Why should tiny seeds be sown shallowly? (2 marks)

26. Explain four ways in which wild animals help people or the environment. (4 marks)

27. Explain how compost conserves both soil and the environment. (5 marks)

28. How can you tell that compost is ready for use? (3 marks)

29. Explain what drip irrigation is. (2 marks)

30. Explain how an improved jiko saves fuel. (3 marks)

31. Describe how to prepare a fine seedbed in three steps. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — It attracts rats and flies and smells bad
   Meat and fatty food attract pests and create a bad smell.

2. C — Plastic bags
   Plastic does not rot and spoils the compost.

3. C — To let in air and mix the materials
   Mixing brings outer material to the middle so all rots evenly.

4. D — Organic
   Organic means it comes from plants and animals.

5. C — Water goes close to the roots so little is wasted
   Only the soil near the plant is wet, so less water is lost.

6. D — Early morning or late afternoon
   The sun is less hot, so less water evaporates.

7. D — Letting water fall slowly drop by drop near the roots
   Drip irrigation gives small amounts of water directly at the roots.

8. B — Fewer weeds grow between plants
   The soil between plants stays dry so fewer weeds grow.

9. A — Gas
   LPG gas is stored under pressure in a cylinder.

10. D — It makes a lot of smoke and gives little heat
   Wet wood wastes heat drying itself.

11. C — Plant trees on their own land and replace those cut
   Growing trees keeps a supply of wood.

12. A — Close the cylinder valve and open windows and doors
   Fire near a gas leak can cause an explosion.

13. D — The top of the pole
   The head is fixed to the top of the long pole.

14. D — A learner who reports poaching to a wildlife officer
   Reporting poaching helps protect animals.

15. C — Birds also eat harmful insects and are part of nature
   Wild animals are needed for balance in nature.

16. C — A hammer or heavy stone to push it in
   An adult helps with heavy or sharp work.

17. D — Watering can with a fine rose
   Fine spray does not wash seeds away.

18. B — Carrot
   Carrots are sown directly because transplanting damages their roots.

19. C — To spread them thinly and evenly
   Sand helps prevent clumps of seeds.

20. B — They take water, light and food from the crop
   Weeds compete with crops.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Plastic and glass, because they do not rot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two items, 1 mark for the reason.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: It gives water near the roots so little is wasted, and less water evaporates because only a small patch of soil is wet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: They are part of nature and biodiversity, and they help in other ways such as pollinating and eating pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: Sowing seeds straight into the place where the crop will grow until harvest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sowing seeds where the crop stays, 1 mark for no transplanting.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: They have little stored food so they cannot push up through deep soil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for little food, 1 mark for not reaching the surface.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Birds eat insects; bees pollinate; animals spread seeds; wildlife brings tourists and money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: It adds food to the soil and makes it firm so it is not washed easily. It reuses wastes instead of leaving them as rubbish, and it reduces the need for factory fertiliser.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for soil, 2 marks for environment, 1 mark for a clear example.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is dark brown, crumbly, smells like earth, and the original wastes cannot be seen.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sign.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is watering plants slowly, drop by drop, next to their roots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for slowly or drop by drop, 1 mark for near the roots.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: Its walls keep the heat close to the pot, so food cooks faster, and less charcoal or wood is used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for heat close to pot, 1 mark for faster cooking, 1 mark for less fuel.

31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear weeds and stones; dig and loosen the soil; break the lumps with a rake until fine and level (add compost).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.
